findings.text: The `item` struct drops `line` and stops filling `val` for `itemError`; error text now lives in `err` and the position in `pos`. This patch doesn't touch the parser. Any consumer that reads `it.line` (for example `p.line = it.line`) or `it.val` for `itemError` will fail to compile or report empty error messages. The unchanged `parse.go` is the likely victim.

`column()` uses `pos+ll >= Start`, which should be `>`. When an error starts at the first byte of a line (for example a control character at column 0 of line 2), `pos+ll == Start` matches the previous line. The column becomes `len(prevLine)+1` instead of 0, so the caret and column range are drawn in the wrong place.
